root_cause: Required proved the complete Netlify production build before merge, but production deployment rebuilt the same source tree again. The build command was also duplicated across Netlify production, deploy-preview and Required, so optimization and ordering drifted independently. A second control-plane defect made shallow exact-SHA Required checkouts fail before the build: material-writeback closure used a three-dot BASE...HEAD diff and therefore required a merge base that a bounded shallow checkout does not need to contain. Admission then exposed a classifier taxonomy gap: product-led website regression tests were not assigned to the website lane even though they verify production/preview website build architecture.
prevention: Use one canonical measured build runner, cache its exact source-tree output, publish that output as a short-lived immutable GitHub artifact, and allow production to reuse it only when a successful Required run and the current main tree SHA match exactly. Production executes only release-identity stamping before provider packaging; any mismatch falls back to the canonical source build. Material-writeback scope detection must use the exact two-tree diff BASE HEAD; merge-base ancestry is not part of this closure contract. Product-led website contract tests are explicitly classified under the website lane and regression-guarded.
